source.title: Criteria and Bias of Parameterized Linear Regression under Edge of Stability Regime

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper empirically and theoretically tests whether large-step gradient descent can converge in an edge-of-stability regime, using quadratic-parameterized linear regression and interpolation residuals. It does not test the listed versions’ stated benchmark, architecture, or training-error measures.
record.gate_note: The results concern regression interpolation and edge-of-stability behavior, not training classification error on CIFAR benchmarks. The paper also discusses related results from other work; those cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests V5's full-batch edge-of-stability behavior in a new network setting: depth-2 diagonal linear networks with squared loss. It measures training residuals, loss and Hessian sharpness, and establishes convergence under specified conditions. These results bear on V5 even though they do not reproduce the wide-network catapult experiment or compare learning rates with the initial linearized model's stability limit.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that quadratic sample loss can coexist with EoS convergence in quadratically parameterized linear regression under specified conditions. Their convergence theory focuses on the restricted one-sample d = 2 setting; the multi-sample extension is empirical. Quadratic sample loss does not make the objective quadratic in the trainable parameters.
record.recipe_differences: Studies one-sample or multi-sample regression with quadratic parameterization and quadratic loss, using residual interpolation and edge-of-stability behavior rather than benchmark classification training error.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome depends on step-size, dimension, input and target degeneracy, initialization scale, and, in the one-sample theory, the relation between μ η and 1. In the multi-sample experiments, overparameterization and non-degeneracy matter.

fits_no_version.finding: The intermediate oscillatory phase lasts proportionally to log(1/α) in the reported experiment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization scale controls the delay before convergence in large-step diagonal linear regression.

fits_no_version.finding: Sparse-prior recovery improves as α approaches zero when μη < 1, but a step-size-dependent recovery error persists when μη > 1 and α² is sufficiently small.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large-step diagonal linear regression has distinct implicit-bias regimes separated by μη = 1.

record.problems: The empirical results are largely presented in figures without tabulated numerical values. The multi-sample evidence is empirical; the stated theorems focus on d = 2 and impose restrictive assumptions, including a one-sparse prior and specific initialization.
record.rows_left_out: No separately recoverable numerical figure values are available in the supplied text. All identified textual outcomes were retained; cited results from other papers were excluded.

untested.parts: Convolutional-network training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random labels, size effects and regularized recipes.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student spurious minima and the benefit of one or two extra student neurons.
Depth degradation in plain convolutional networks, identity shortcuts, deep tanh initialization and Fixup.
Activation-matched initialization, propagation across layers, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights and trainable depth.

The wide-network catapult setting; learning rates measured relative to the initial linearized-model stability limit; and runs shown to diverge despite starting below that threshold. The study's transient threshold crossing does not establish prolonged hovering.
Batch-normalization comparisons, accuracy gain per training time, learning-rate tolerance with versus without normalization, and Fixup comparisons.

missing.what: Conditional theoretical convergence results: Theorem 1 assumes eventual residual sign alternation and μη < 1; Theorem 2 establishes eventual linear convergence for restricted μη > 1, small initialization and 0 < |x| < 1/(μη). Proposition 1 gives a further conditional asymptotic result. These are not captured by the empirical rows.
Separate the input-dependent failure condition from the step-size sweep: for sufficiently large x, GD does not converge when μη > 1. R5 currently obscures this condition.
missing.locator: Figure 3 caption; Section 3; Appendix A.4, Lemma 13

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V5. Its network parameterization and direct loss/sharpness measurements justify V5 links, while its initialization-duration and sparse-recovery findings fit none of the listed versions. No reported control establishes the specific below-initial-threshold divergence clause.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error, corrupted or random labels, model size, and training duration.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual convolutional networks, depth effects, shortcuts, and normalization.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, and trainable depth.
The stated wide-network setting and comparisons to the initial linearized-model stability limit, sharpness hovering over longer training, and divergence from below threshold.
Batch normalization comparisons on MNIST, CIFAR-10, or ImageNet, and Fixup comparisons.

rows.subject: one-sample parameterized linear regression with quadratic loss
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent with a large constant step-size; reports residual oscillation and convergence in the edge-of-stability regime.
rows.measure: Residual trajectory and sharpness relative to 2/η
rows.baseline: GF regime: residual magnitude decreases monotonically and sharpness remains under 2/η
rows.value: EoS: residual oscillates and changes sign; sharpness first exceeds 2/η and decreases
rows.note: The result concerns regression residual and sharpness, not classification error.
rows.check: Figure 1 and Section 3 show convergence after sharpness exceeds 2/η, but sharpness subsequently falls below that threshold rather than persistently hovering there. Figure 1 itself plots weights, objective and scaled sharpness; the residual description comes from Section 3.

rows.measure: Whether EoS occurs and whether gradient descent diverges
rows.value: EoS does not occur; gradient descent diverges

rows.subject: one-sample parameterized linear regression
rows.operation_detail: Sweeps step-size to show transitions among gradient-flow, edge-of-stability subregimes, chaos, and divergence.
rows.value: Increasing step-size gives different EoS subregimes, then chaos and divergence; for μ η < 1 the oscillation envelope shrinks, while for μ η > 1 it can expand before convergence or reach a periodic orbit
rows.locator: Figure 3 and its caption; Section 3, “Effect of step-size and types of oscillation”
rows.note: The plotted step-size values are not assigned in the flattened figure text.
rows.check: This row combines convergent EoS, intermediate periodic behavior, persistent nonconvergence, chaos and divergence. Split these conditions. For suitable x, the intermediate periodic phase is followed by convergence; for sufficiently large x and μη > 1, convergence fails. μη = 1 is not identified as the initial linearized-model stability threshold.

rows.subject: one-sample parameterized linear regression
rows.operation_detail: Varies initialization scale and compares the limiting solution’s distance from the sparse prior across step-size regimes.
rows.value: Error decreases almost linearly in α and recovers the sparse solution as α tends to 0
rows.locator: Figure 5 and its caption; Section 3, “Effect of α, sparsity and generalization error”
rows.note: The text describes the trend; figure values are not transcribed.
rows.check: Distance from the limiting interpolator to a sparse prior measures implicit bias and parameter recovery, not a behavior named in V1–V6.

rows.subject: one-sample parameterized linear regression
rows.operation_detail: Varies initialization scale and compares the limiting solution’s distance from the sparse prior across step-size regimes.
rows.value: Error is decided by η regardless of α and does not recover the sparse solution as α tends to 0
rows.locator: Figure 5 and its caption; Section 3, “Effect of α, sparsity and generalization error”
rows.note: The text states this qualified trend for small α.
rows.check: Failure to recover the sparse prior is an implicit-bias result, not incomplete training convergence. A nonsparse limiting solution can still interpolate the training sample.
